title: Owlkei Go Concurrency Model
purpose: Document thread safety guarantees and race conditions

http_request_model.synchronization: implicit (each request gets own context object from pool)

websocket_connection_model.synchronization: channelized (readLoop → handler → memorybroker.Publish → writeLoop via channel)

app container (internal/core/container.g.description: per-app providers, layers, routes, events and handler plans
app container (internal/core/container.g.access: written during app.Create() on the calling goroutine; with AsyncImports, the background wiring adds providers and module states under container.mu (RWMutex), one wiring goroutine at a time (wireMu); everything a request reads without a gate stays immutable after Create
app container (internal/core/container.g.synchronization: immutable after initialization; two apps never share one

trace.Tracer.description: Typed trace listeners of one app (replaces the removed event bus)
trace.Tracer.synchronization: immutable listener slice behind an atomic.Pointer; Enabled and Emit take no lock; Listen and stop copy the slice under one mutex

accesslog.AccessLog.description: Access log listener; no goroutine of its own
accesslog.AccessLog.access: listener on request goroutines; the complete event logs the line on the emitting goroutine; Stop at shutdown
accesslog.AccessLog.synchronization: 64 shards (sync.Mutex + map + eviction list each), the line logged after the shard lock is released, atomic stopped flag

memorycache.MemoryCache.description: Bounded in-memory cache (default backend of modules/cache and the throttler); no goroutine of its own
memorycache.MemoryCache.access: any goroutine; the sweep runs on a short-lived runtime goroutine of a time.AfterFunc armed only while an entry with a ttl exists
memorycache.MemoryCache.synchronization: 64 shards, each a sync.RWMutex over its index map, entry array, free list, CLOCK hand and counters (Get / TTL / Keys read lock, writes write lock, never two shard locks); reference marks are uint32 through sync/atomic, hits / misses atomic per shard; a sync.Mutex guards the sweep's armed / dirty flags and timer, taken only while no shard lock is held

config.ConfigService.description: Configuration shared by every injected copy
config.ConfigService.access: Get / Transform from any goroutine at any time; Set from any goroutine (meant for hooks)
config.ConfigService.synchronization: atomic.Pointer to an immutable map; Set copies the map under a sync.Mutex and stores the new pointer (copy on write)

logpipe.Sink.description: Output pipeline of the built-in logger (one per output; stdout is process-wide)
logpipe.Sink.access: callers append records; at most one writer goroutine, alive only while it writes; in async mode it starts 1 ms after the first record of a burst (one reusable time.AfterFunc timer whose goroutine becomes the writer), at once at 16 KiB queued, on Fatal or while a Flush waits; idle = no goroutine and no pending timer
logpipe.Sink.synchronization: one sync.Mutex over two swapped buffers, counters, flags, the wake timer (Reset / Stop under the lock) and the waiting-Flush count; the writing flag decides who writes, a stale timer fire costs at most one early pass; waiters on a channel closed after each batch; never held during the output's Write; Snapshot() (inspect.Snapshotter) takes it once

memorybroker.Broker.synchronization: single sync.RWMutex over 4 maps, no sharding; PublishAsync additionally coordinates via sync.WaitGroup so Close() can drain in-flight async goroutines before clearing state

module_state.description: Module configuration, providers and pending / ready / failed state (internal/core/module_state.go, module_async.go)
module_state.access: read-only after app.Create() for modules ready then; AsyncImports entries are built on one goroutine each (ended when settled), wiring serialized by wireMu, factories outside it
module_state.synchronization: status and attempts are atomics; settle is first-call-wins; a gated module's routes and events open by one atomic.Pointer Store of a fully built table (the happens-before edge); lock order wireMu → mu, never held while user code runs except wireMu around OnInit / NewProvider / NewController / OnReady; a stopping flag under mu stops wiring at shutdown

owlkei.Retry.synchronization: no goroutine of its own: one time.Timer stopped on return; reports attempts and the next retry time to the entry through atomics

not_thread_safe.handler_closures: if handler captures mutable state, not thread-safe
not_thread_safe.controller_state: if controller has mutable fields, not thread-safe
not_thread_safe.provider_state: if provider has mutable fields, not thread-safe
not_thread_safe.module_state_during_init: module is mutable during app.Create(), must not call Create() concurrently

concurrency_guarantees.http_request: each request is fully isolated, no race conditions possible
concurrency_guarantees.ws_connection: each connection is single-threaded, no race conditions within connection
concurrency_guarantees.message_broker: concurrent-safe pub/sub via a single RWMutex; not lock-free (RWMutex-guarded, not literally atomic ops)

scenario_1.name: Retaining context after request
scenario_1.description: Handler stores context reference, reused in next request
scenario_1.prevention: never hold onto context after handler returns

scenario_2.name: Mutable provider state
scenario_2.description: Provider with mutable fields shared across requests
scenario_2.example: type Service struct { counter int }; counter++ in handler
scenario_2.prevention: use sync.Mutex if mutable state needed, or make stateless

scenario_3.name: Raw websocket access
scenario_3.description: Handler writes directly to conn, fanout also writes
scenario_3.impact: concurrent writes to connection, message corruption
scenario_3.example: conn.Send() in handler while fanout sends
scenario_3.prevention: use Publisher only, never raw conn access

scenario_4.name: Module mutation during Create
scenario_4.example: Create() called from two goroutines simultaneously
scenario_4.prevention: Create() must be called exactly once, before any requests

memory_safety.message_broker: lightweight pub/sub (no message buffering except WS send channels)

deadlock_risks.risk_2: memorybroker.Broker.Close() called synchronously from within a handler that was itself dispatched by PublishAsync — self-deadlock, VERIFIED (see anti-patterns-gotchas.md). Close()'s wg.Wait() can never return because wg.Done() for that goroutine only runs after the handler (which is blocked in Close()) returns. NOT a bug in the locking, an inherent property of waiting on your own in-flight WaitGroup entry; documented as unsupported rather than special-cased
deadlock_risks.risk_2_note: Reentrancy is otherwise SAFE and verified by test: a handler calling Subscribe/Unsubscribe/Publish/PublishAsync (including on itself) does not deadlock, because publishInternal releases its RLock before invoking any handler — Close() called from a SYNC Publish handler is also safe (Publish isn't WaitGroup-tracked)
deadlock_risks.risk_3: A trace listener blocking on I/O (listeners run synchronously on the request goroutine)
deadlock_risks.prevention: keep pipeline stages lock-free and non-blocking; never call Close() synchronously from a PublishAsync-dispatched handler

cancellation_handling.http_requests: No per-request ctx.HTTPContext.SetDeadline()/Deadline/IsDeadlineExceeded() exists; do not invent them. Timeouts are server-level internal defaults (internal/core/server.go newServerDefaults): ReadHeaderTimeout 5s, ReadTimeout 30s, WriteTimeout 30s, IdleTimeout 75s; a handler extends its own with http.NewResponseController. During a shutdown each running request's Context() is cancelled when ShutdownTimeout passes.
cancellation_handling.graceful_shutdown: Built in (internal/core/server.go): SIGINT/SIGTERM or app.Stop() -> stop intercepting signals -> close the listener and idle connections -> drain running requests for ServerOptions.ShutdownTimeout (default 30s) -> runShutdownHooks() once per app (shutdownOnce): every Module's OnShutdown in the exact reverse of the init order, a panicking hook logged as OnShutdownPanic -> access log stopped. Stop() is safe from any goroutine; called from a handler it waits for that request (use go app.Stop()). No WebSocket-specific shutdown: open WS connections end when the process exits.
